title: Cold rebuild: find the pods that are not ready
summary: Read pod states on a real Kubernetes cluster, from memory, no hints.

steps.title: Cold rebuild
body: Time to prove a skill stuck. In *kubectl basics* you read a namespace's pods on a real cluster and said which ones were
not ready, and why. Now do it again from memory: the same scenario, **no hints, no solution to peek at**. The checks
are exactly the ones you passed the first time.
Why: pulling something out of memory is what makes it stay there. Reading your old commands feels like knowing
them; doing it cold shows whether you do. If you get stuck, that is useful news: go back to the lesson,
then come back and try again tomorrow.
This check, plus the boss, is what proves the module.

steps.prompt: A container restarts every minute. `kubectl logs web-1` shows only the startup banner of the *new* attempt. How do you see the output of the attempt that crashed?
steps.explain: `--previous` (or `-p`) shows the logs of the last terminated container instance, which is usually where the stack trace is.

steps.title: Find the pods that are not ready, cold
prompt: This terminal runs a **real one-node Kubernetes 1.37 cluster** (k3s) with `kubectl` (alias `k`).
1. write the names of the pods that are not ready (a `Completed` pod is fine) into `~/answers/notready.txt`;
2. write one line per not-ready pod into `~/answers/reasons.txt`, `NAME REASON`, REASON one of `readiness`,
From memory: no hints this time.
